notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); the gate raised no warning. Model-authored and unreviewed: nothing ran on an arm, and the R1 hardware backend opens a TCP socket to the controller only when an operator passes it with allow_hardware. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card's helper is PythonObjectDriver (python-object family); this is a direct Driver over the SDK's transport class dobot_sdk.core.connection:DobotConnection, because the upstream builds every command from parts (dobot_sdk/api/motion.py:31-46, :52-87) and assembles its own argument lists, which a command table cannot reproduce; the command text is copied from the upstream builders and never re-spelled. NOT COVERED: joint velocity and jog commands (MoveJog, ServoJ, ServoP), the relative and ARC/Circle moves, the IO and Modbus modules (io.*, communication.*), the feedback-monitor status of DobotRobot.GetStatus (joint and Cartesian state are read with GetAngle/GetPose instead), the HTTP error texts of ErrorController (only the controller's numeric error ids are read), and the script/plugin control commands. The controller exposes no completion signal for a queued move, so reached is the driver's read-back criterion (0.01 degree per joint, 1 mm for the tool position) and not a device tolerance; a non-blocking joint move reports the state read once. The stop action accepts the class's deceleration input but the controller's Stop() takes no deceleration argument (robot_control.py:83-85), so a value is documented as not sent. Joint travel and the Cartesian workspace are operator_required (the clone states no numbers), so the package ships site-limits.example.json and refuses every move with MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the site fills it. Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-29; reviewed_by stays null): accepted after reviewer edits: risk raised from R1 to R2 (a six-axis arm is moving machinery, as the xArm exemplar), with the controller's emergency-stop button as estop_physical_ref (the vendor's safety note, assets/SDK_API文档_完整版.md:2384); native.py and facts.md now say so, and the hardware backend waits for a human signature. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
